Hope you’re well. We're reviewing vendors ahead of a procurement sprint and I have a few quick questions about how Redwood handles tracking on the hosted console and website, and how that ties into the DPA/subprocessor commitments:

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear list. I'll loop in legal + engineering and share the relevant docs. High level:

- We do use analytics on our marketing site and product console, but the console telemetry is logically separated from marketing analytics and is configurable by customers.
- Redwood does not use customer-provided content (model prompts/outputs) for marketing profiling. Product telemetry we keep aggregated/hashed; sensitive fields are redacted prior to storage.
- We have an up-to-date DPA and a maintained subprocessors list; transfers from the EU can be covered via SCCs or we can offer EU-region hosting for most customers.

Hi Olivia / Tom,

Thanks for reaching out. Attaching the current DPA (DPA_Redwood_v2.pdf), the canonical subprocessors list (Subprocessors_2026-01.csv), and a short Cookie & Telemetry FAQ (Cookie_and_Telemetry_FAQ.pdf). Key points below for your privacy review: 

1) Cookies & Marketing Analytics (marketing website)
- We use a self-hosted analytics stack (Matomo) for our marketing site by default; no third-party marketing pixels are embedded on the console by default. Marketing analytics are pseudonymized and aggregated; retention defaults to 13 months.
- Customers can request suppression of marketing analytics for their account in writing; we record an audit trail.

2) Console telemetry & API usage
- Console and API telemetry are used for product operations (performance, error triage, usage trends). We do not use raw customer prompt/response content for marketing.
- Telemetry pipeline applies automated PII detection and redaction (email addresses, API keys, tokens) before long-term storage. Short-term debug traces are ephemeral and scoped to SRE access.

3) Subprocessors and transfers
- Subprocessors list covers CDN, observability, and a hosted analytics provider (self-hosted hosting partner). The CSV has hostnames and transfer locations.
- For EEA transfers, we rely on EU SCCs by default and also offer the option to restrict processing to EU-hosted infra where available (Redwood Private / regional Dedicated).

4) Consent & admin controls
- Console admin has toggles to opt out of non-essential telemetry and to enable stricter retention. We surface a cookie banner on the marketing site; the console shows an admin privacy controls page for account owners.

If useful, we can provide a DPA redline template. I've attached the artifacts; please review and tell us if you prefer a redline or an executed PDF + DocuSign.

Best,

Hi all — quick tech addendum from engineering about how the console & telemetry behave today: 

- Cookies: console uses a small set of first-party cookies for session management (rw_sid, expires 14d) and a non-essential cookie (rw_analytics, expires 90d) that is only set after admin consent. The marketing site sets a separate Matomo cookie for aggregate analytics.

- Telemetry pipeline: console -> edge proxy -> telemetry collector -> scrubber -> storage. The scrubber applies regex-based PII filters + schema-based redaction (we never persist API keys or full prompt text unless the customer enables debug mode and consents).

- Admin controls: Organization admins can disable rw_analytics and toggle ‘Limit telemetry retention’ which sets retention to 30 days and removes IP granularity. For Dedicated/Private deployments we can disable external analytics integrations entirely.

- Implementation notes for Acme: we can provide a console-config bundle that disables marketing cookies by default and enforces telemetry retention at 30 days. Jordan attached a short config snippet in the shared Drive link.

Let me know if you want a quick tech walkthrough.
